title: Armenian Eucharistic book states: ancestral witnesses, Roman editions and Catholic reception

traditions.label: Armenian ancestral witnesses
traditions.scope: Earlier Armenian anaphora and printed service-book witnesses.
traditions.coverage_note: Antecedents and comparanda; these are not retrospectively labelled received Armenian Catholic books.

traditions.label: Armenian Catholic book states
traditions.scope: Roman Armenian editions and later Armenian Catholic reception and reform.
traditions.coverage_note: Rite identity remains Armenian. Publication in Rome, Latin parallel text and Western additions do not turn the complete book into a Latin-rite Roman Missal.

traditions.label: Lviv Armenian manuscript reception
traditions.scope: One composite manuscript, its base copying and subsequent corrections.
traditions.coverage_note: Local reception evidenced by the San Lazzaro catalogue; no universal Armenian use or precise date of correction inferred.

traditions.label: Armenian Apostolic textual witnesses
traditions.scope: Seventeenth-century printing described as preserving Apostolic textual tradition.
traditions.coverage_note: Printer affiliation is distinct from the text and its Roman reception.

sources.title: Ninel Voskanian et al., Հայ գիրքը 1512–1800 թվականներին (Yerevan, 1988)
sources.inspection: Complete PDF acquired; page images read: printed p. 3/PDF 59, entry 2; p. 25/PDF 81, entry 34; p. 79/PDF 135, entries 103–104, including entry 103 continuation at top right. Addendum 2026-10-22: PDF p. 135 re-rendered at 200–500 dpi and entries 103–104 read whole. Entry 103: [2], 20, 30 (= 52) two-column pages, second title at the start of the second pagination, type area 25.3 × 16.3 cm, four woodcuts on [ii], p. 3, p. 10 and second-sequence p. 2. Entry 104: 50 two-column pages with the second title on p. 21 (continuous pagination), type area 24 × 16 cm, four woodcuts, contents as entry 103; its note reports that, although the book bears 1677, G. Zarbhanalian and A. Ghazikian held it to have been printed much later by a vardapet Gevorg (surname read as Paghtatean, uncertain).
sources.limitations: Bibliographical descriptions, not a diplomatic edition. Entry 104 carries a warning that its 1677 imprint may conceal later production. Full protected catalogue retained only as research scratch. Entry 104's later dating is the compilers' report of two earlier bibliographers, not an inspected copy or a dated colophon.

sources.title: Կարգեալ սուրբ խորհուրդ պատարագի հայոց / Ordo divinae missae Armenorum (Rome: Propaganda Fide, 1642)
sources.inspection: All 148 available page IDs acquired as images. Visually read title PP5 and Creed sequence PA46–PA49, both Armenian and facing Latin. PA46 image has printed numeral 49 and PA49 image numeral 46; PA47 and PA48 have matching numerals. Read the transition from Creed Amen directly to the doxology on printed p. 48. Front matter PP7/artifact 7 inspected: Vincentius Riccardus dates the review/emendation certificate Rome 6 May 1636. PP8/artifact 8 is Giovanni Molino’s undated Italian certificate comparing Latin and Armenian; PP9/artifact 9 has two imprimaturs. These are front matter, not a terminal colophon. Original title remains Rome 1642.
sources.limitations: Whole book acquired but not wholly read or transcribed. Google page IDs and printed pagination must both be retained. The work is an Armenian liturgy edited in Rome, not thereby a Roman-rite missal.

sources.title: Խորհրդատետր պատարագին հայոց / Lyturgia Armena; Սպասաւորութիւն պատարագի / Ministerium Missae (Rome, 1677), Biblioteca Angelica copy
sources.inspection: All 96 provider images acquired. Native Lyturgia pp. 1–20 and Ministerium pp. 1–30 visually surveyed; exact bounded Creed/anathema loci compared with 1823. Lyturgia title is artifact 41, printed pp. 1–2 are vesting prayers at 43–44; printed pp. 4–5 appear twice at 46–47 and 48–49. Printed p. 8 is artifact 52 / RA1-PP14. Ministerium service text pp. 2–19 precedes blank p. 20, Office corrections pp. 21–24 and hymnal corrections pp. 25–30. Whole PDF SHA-256 5f0b9eb92edbc3b2028e72e5017158be1942d89603917e1c00feca490f4462bc recomputed and matched. Addendum 2026-10-21: Lyturgia p. 8 (Google RA1-PP14) re-fetched at 1600-pixel width; its left column shows the same three Creed readings as Venice 1823 pp. 40–41 (before all ages, consubstantial, procession from the Father and the Son).
sources.limitations: Native pages were structurally surveyed, not exhaustively transcribed or word-collated. The Latin Codex is a separately titled expression, not the native textual control. Repeated scan leaves do not create extra liturgical text or a different impression. A separate 20 October 2026 review completed all 18 offered EAP180/1/1/12 source frames at native JPEG-region detail and established its exact item-specific CC BY-NC 4.0 grant. That separate FSL A/711 witness is candidate arm-1677-liturgia-eap-fsl-19-page-setting and canonical edition edition.armenian-church.lyturgia-armena.1677-rome-propaganda-19-page-setting. Its liturgy ends at printed 19, followed by corrections 21–30, unlike this Google 20-page Lyturgia and separate Ministerium. Distinct pp. 8 and 10 settings and endings prevent silent substitution. Original TIFF/JP2 masters, physical/intact-text completeness and qualified Armenian transcription remain unestablished. This source entry and its existing stage still refer to the Google-controlled witness; no new stage, recension or ancestry is admitted. Addendum 2026-10-22: this Angelica/Google copy matches bibliography entry 103 exactly (collation [2], 20, 30; woodcuts at artifacts 42, 45, 54 and 68 = [ii], p. 3, p. 10 and Ministerium p. 2).

sources.title: Lyturgia Armena (Rome, 1677), Fundamental Scientific Library Yerevan A/711, British Library EAP180/1/1/12
sources.inspection: Registered 19-page facsimile (SHA-256 e3c221aa50bd46721be3cfe337c8f2b183a8ae4003bc78dd410019e1daa8fa12) viewed frame by frame on 2026-10-22 and compared with the Google 1677 copy at the same scale: title (frame 2) and p. 1 (frame 3, signature A2) line for line; pp. 2–6 by layout; p. 7 Creed column (frame 6) read at native resolution; pp. 9–11 (frames 7–8) with signatures; p. 19 terminus (frame 12); correction p. 21 (frame 13) line for line against Google Ministerium p. 21.
sources.limitations: A mixed copy, remounted and repaired: the title, pp. 1–6 and the correction gathering pp. 21–30 (signature D) are the same settings as the Google copy; pp. 7–19 are a different setting (the Creed starts on p. 7 instead of p. 8, no full-page Crucifixion woodcut on p. 10, signature B on p. 9 where Google has B on p. 7 and B2 on p. 9, liturgy ending on p. 19 before a blank [20]). The Ministerium title and service pages are absent from the offered frames. No word-level collation beyond the Creed; who reset pp. 7–19, and when, is not evidenced on the pages.

sources.title: Խորհրդատետր սրբոյ Պատարագին ըստ արարողութեան Հայաստանեայց եկեղեցւոյ համեմատ օրինակին տպելոյ ի Հռովմ 1677 (Venice: San Lazzaro, 1823), University of Michigan copy
sources.inspection: All 88 provider images acquired; title PA1/artifact 5 names Rome 1677 as exemplar. All printed pp. 5–80 visually surveyed against the native 1677 booklets. Creed, Nicene anathema and doxology occur pp. 40–41; institution narrative p. 50; epiclesis and bread/cup blessing pp. 51–53; Gospel bodies pp. 69–70; dismissal p. 71; Alleluia appendix pp. 72–80. Final six words of the anathema at p. 41/artifact 45 agree with 1677 p. 8/artifact 52 after line-wrap and punctuation normalization. Whole PDF SHA-256 81812bd4c2895111788582de47144fabb2500f9f923b22bb441274cbee7a8bb6 recomputed and matched. Addendum 2026-10-21: pp. 40–41 re-fetched at 1600-pixel width (Google pg=PA40, PA41) and read: the Son article has միածին նախ քան զամենայն յաւիտեանս and համագոյակից Հօր; the Spirit article includes որ ՚ի Հօրէ եւ յՈրդւոյ բղխի (procession from the Father and the Son); the anathema and doxology follow on p. 41.
sources.limitations: Whole retained sequence structurally surveyed; no exhaustive verbal identity or new normative reform established. Expanded Psalm/Gospel bodies and added supporting sections are changes in printed extent. This Michigan 80-page format is not automatically identical to the LOC exhibition copy.

sources.inspection: Retained 228-page PDF (SHA-256 b57d49313c53c9909f4adb590abb5eae4ec0fc4955339c7a13a8f049b42facd3) from the 2026-10-19 Armenian lane. Visually read on 2026-10-21: title PDF p. 5; the declaration Յայտարարութիւն PDF pp. 6–7, its closing paragraph re-rendered at 200–300 dpi; the fourth day of the Nativity, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 12, left page), with its Psalm, Epistle and Gospel headings; index PDF pp. 219–225 surveyed. sources.title: Խորհրդատետր Սուրբ Պատարագի աշխարհաբար թարգմանութեամբ. Թիւ Սուրբ Պատարագ (Zmmar: Armenian Catholic Patriarchate, 2007), patriarchate PDF
sources.inspection: 168-page PDF retained from the 2026-10-20 coverage-closure lane (SHA-256 0ae51fefe1924c6e677cdb5a4d7c640840e887ada099b26c66032d9369f2b48b). On 2026-10-21 the legacy ArmSCII-8 text layer was decoded for searching and the cited pages were checked as rendered images: title PDF p. 3; credits PDF p. 4 (commission work, patriarchal publication, Zmmar, 10 October 2006); patriarchal decree 279/06 of 7 November 2006, PDF p. 6 (printed 7); introduction PDF pp. 8–9 (printed 9–10), stating that the translation is printed beside the classical text; classical Creed and doxology on PDF pp. 41, 43 and 45 (printed 42, 44, 46); commemoration of the Pope in the classical intercessions, PDF p. 87 (printed 88).

sources.title: Eton College B44637, Codex mysterij missae Armenorum, seu Lyturgia armena (1677)
sources.inspection: Full catalogue HTML read: language, collation, contents, copy notes and possible issue with Armenian Lyturgia.
sources.limitations: Catalogue identifies the Latin translation, [2], 37, [1] pages; it is distinct from the native Armenian 20+30-page set. Not an independent Armenian recension.

sources.title: Anna Ohanjanyan, Creedal Controversies among Armenians in the Seventeenth-Century Ottoman Empire, JSAS 27 (2020), 7–69, DOI 10.1163/26670038-12342708
sources.inspection: Article pp. 15–16 and 39, including notes 25–26 and 119–121, read in extracted text and checked against PDF page images 19, 20, 43. Full issue acquired for research.
sources.limitations: P. 39/n. 121 dates the early Ordo to 1646. The inspected 1642 title and Creed independently establish the before-state used here; the article date is not silently corrected. The 1686 reception account depends on Djemdjemian 1989, pp. 154–155, 173–179. Note 121 (read in extracted text 2026-10-21) cites the 1646 Ordo at pp. 46–49 and describes the 1636 review by Vincentius Riccardus and Molino’s licence, matching the inspected 1642 book’s Creed pages and front matter.

sources.title: San Lazzaro manuscript catalogue, no. 669 (old 1178), ԺՈՂՈՎԱԾՈՅ ԽԱ
sources.inspection: Complete native Armenian HTML record read: colophons, 1636 date, inferred Lviv origin, contents item 22/Mass fol. 263, lectionary additions fols. 476b2–478a1, and description of corrections conforming to Rome 1677.
sources.limitations: No manuscript images supplied or read. HTML has damaged folio notation (2631) and other typographical defects. Catalogue attributes Lviv use; it does not date the correcting hands. Acquisition by San Lazzaro before 1791 is not a proven terminus for every annotation.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Armenian Literary Tradition exhibition, items 010–012
sources.inspection: Native titles and English descriptions read for 1722 manuscript, 1823 print and 1887 Bianchini chant manuscript; 1823 opening spread image viewed.
sources.limitations: The loose English caption Roman Catholic rite is read with the native title identifying the Armenian Church. Display images are selected openings, not complete books. No Catholic reception established for the 1722 manuscript.

sources.title: Michael Daniel Findikyan, Armenian Liturgy, New Catholic Encyclopedia
sources.inspection: Full article read; especially Divine Liturgy paragraphs on Xosrov, medieval anaphoras and late introduction/conclusion, plus bibliography (b).
sources.limitations: Expert synthesis identifies the commentary witness; manuscript and critical edition remain uninspected. Its broad developmental claims do not supply a continuous dated book genealogy.

sources.title: F. E. Brightman, Liturgies Eastern and Western I (Oxford, 1896), introduction, The Armenian liturgies
sources.inspection: Printed xcvii–xcix (PDF pp. 99–101 of the registered 714-page scan, SHA-256 254f7d21b44436bdbac565b6f932d9e38d6ef8a062d9a8d944957e1a5d607ef0) read as page images on 2026-10-21: printed Gregorian and Uniat editions, translations, and manuscript group 1 with its ten liturgies or anaphoras no longer in use.
sources.limitations: Introductory description by the editor; the manuscripts themselves are uninspected and Brightman gives no folio loci or palaeographic discussion. His Rome 1670 and 1686 Uniat editions are unconfirmed by the national bibliography.

sources.title: Movses Tonanian, Հայ եկեղեցւոյ ծէսը և ծիսակարգը, broadcast 54 (Vatican News, 25 June 2021)
sources.inspection: Entire native Armenian article read, especially paragraphs identifying Vienna 1879, synods 1967/1968, May 1987 celebration, 1992 study and Pentecost 1994 implementation; final paragraph cites Աւետիք 1994 p. 365.
sources.limitations: Authorial retrospective on the Vatican communications site, not the decree or edition itself. Its earlier 1676 date conflicts with inspected 1677 imprints. No modern full text imported and no exact modern textual delta inferred.

sources.title: H. Gr. Galemkʻearean, Թուղթ Յովհ. Ա. Կաթողիկեայց, Գլ. Ե. Համար 7, 8, առ Հայս, Handēs Amsōreay 20 (1906), no. 8, pp. 225–234
sources.inspection: Article PDF from the Pan-Armenian Digital Library (https://arar.sci.am/Content/261359/225-234.pdf, SHA-256 d584736a77b78dd4007e59e403173b7363a1f2ce52970b596ea67d815b2939f5) acquired 2026-10-22; pp. 233–234 read on page images at 290 dpi (forms A–D of 1 John 5:7–8 with their manuscript and printed witnesses; reading days of 1 John 5; dated conclusion, Constantinople 9/22 February 1906). The tert.nla.am copy still returned a Cloudflare challenge.
sources.limitations: A survey of the verse in Armenian manuscripts and printings. It names the Hassunian Khorhrdatetr (lection book), Vienna 1879 and 1904, only in its list of reading days: 1 John 5:4–10 on the fourth day of Yaytnutʻiwn (p. 234, right column, item 4); it does not place that book in any of its textual forms. Its conclusion that verse 7 entered Armenian printings through the Vulgate is the author's judgment. Pages 225–232 were not read.

stages.label: Athanasius anaphora in Xosrov’s commentary
stages.scope: The commentary supplies an early textual witness to the Athanasius anaphora.
stages.witness_label: Xosrov Anjewac‘i, Commentary on the Divine Liturgy (author died c. 963)
stages.summary: The commentary supplies an early textual witness to the Athanasius anaphora.

evidence.locus: Divine Liturgy, paragraph beginning The two most important commentaries
evidence.claim: Identifies Xosrov’s phrase-by-phrase commentary as the earliest extant text of the Athanasius anaphora.

stages.limitations: Century placement follows the source, not a dated surviving codex. Earliest manuscript shelfmarks, textual recension and full native text must be established from the critical edition.
stages.reception: Ancestral Armenian witness; Catholic reception is not asserted.

stages.label: Thirteenth-century San Lazzaro liturgy manuscript
stages.scope: The ordinary liturgy under the title of Athanasius together with the Chrysostom, Basil, Presanctified and Roman liturgies, no longer in use.
stages.witness_label: Venice, Bibl. S. Lazzaro, Arm. 1411: Athanasius with Chrysostom, Basil, Presanctified and Roman liturgies
stages.summary: Brightman names this manuscript in the most important group of Armenian liturgy manuscripts. Besides the Athanasius liturgy it contains the complete Chrysostom, Basil and Presanctified liturgies (from the Greek) and the Roman liturgy (from the Latin); unlike Lyon it has none of the further anaphoras.

evidence.locus: Printed xcviii, manuscripts group 1, items (1)–(6); xcix, distinction of anaphoras (5) and (7)–(10) from complete liturgies
evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, its thirteenth-century date and the four further liturgies it contains.

stages.limitations: Manuscript uninspected; the date is Brightman’s and no folio loci are given. A list of contents does not establish the wording of the Athanasius liturgy or any change from the Xosrov witness. Century date only.
stages.reception: Ancestral Armenian witness. The Roman liturgy in Armenian is a translated Latin rite; no Catholic reception of the manuscript is asserted.

stages.label: Lyon manuscript with ten further liturgies
stages.scope: The ordinary liturgy under the title of Athanasius together with translated liturgies and anaphoras no longer in use.
stages.witness_label: Lyon, Bibliothèque municipale, Or. 15: Athanasius with Chrysostom, Basil, Presanctified, James, Ignatius, Roman, Gregory the Illuminator, Gregory Nazianzen, Cyril and Isaac (Sahak)
stages.summary: Brightman names this manuscript among the most important group containing, besides the Athanasius liturgy, liturgies translated from Greek, Syriac and Latin and further anaphoras no longer in use.

evidence.locus: Printed xcviii, manuscripts group 1, and xcix items (7)–(10)
evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, its date and which of the ten further liturgies it contains.

stages.limitations: Manuscript uninspected; the date is Brightman’s and no folio loci are given. A list of contents does not establish the wording of the Athanasius liturgy or any change from the Xosrov witness.
stages.reception: Ancestral Armenian witness. The Roman liturgy in Armenian is a translated Latin rite; no Catholic reception of the manuscript is asserted.

stages.label: Munich manuscript copied from a 1288 exemplar
stages.scope: The ordinary liturgy under the title of Athanasius together with translated liturgies and anaphoras no longer in use.

stages.summary: Brightman names this manuscript among the most important group containing, besides the Athanasius liturgy, liturgies translated from Greek, Syriac and Latin and further anaphoras no longer in use.

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, its date and which of the ten further liturgies it contains.

stages.label: First printed Armenian service-book witness
stages.scope: An early printed Armenian Eucharistic service book, preceding the Roman Catholic editions.
stages.witness_label: Պատարագատետր (Խորհրդատետր), Venice, Hakob Meghapart, 1513; Armenian bibliography entry 2
stages.summary: An early printed Armenian Eucharistic service book, preceding the Roman Catholic editions.

evidence.claim: Identifies the title, colophon, 44-leaf collation and Eucharistic contents.

stages.limitations: Bibliography inspected, book text not collated. Some scholarship debates conversion of the Armenian colophon year; 1513 is the national catalogue’s date. This row records the witness, not a proven new recension.

stages.label: Lviv composite service-book base
stages.scope: Composite service book includes calendar, office, hymns, Mass, lectionary and Gospels; its Mass is attributed to Athanasius.
stages.witness_label: San Lazzaro MS 669 (old 1178), ԺՈՂՈՎԱԾՈՅ ԽԱ; colophon of Anton, 1 June 1636
stages.summary: Composite service book includes calendar, office, hymns, Mass, lectionary and Gospels; its Mass is attributed to Athanasius.

evidence.locus: Colophons, fol. 396a2; contents item 22, fol. 263; lectionary additions fols. 476b2–478a1
evidence.claim: Identifies dated copying and components later bearing corrections.

stages.limitations: 1636 dates a colophon in the composite, not every component or addition; another section bears 1662. Uncorrected readings have not been reconstructed from page images.
stages.reception: Catalogue attributes official daily use to the Lviv Armenian cathedral; location is the cataloguer’s inference.

stages.label: Roman edition with Western-form Creed
stages.scope: Armenian liturgy in Armenian and Latin columns. Its Creed follows the Western form and passes directly to the doxology without the Nicene anathema.
stages.witness_label: Կարգեալ սուրբ խորհուրդ պատարագի հայոց / Ordo divinae missae Armenorum, Rome 1642
stages.summary: Armenian liturgy in Armenian and Latin columns. Its Creed follows the Western form and passes directly to the doxology without the Nicene anathema.

evidence.locus: Title PP5; PA46–PA49, especially printed p. 48
evidence.claim: The 1642 imprint and Creed-to-doxology sequence are directly visible.
Identifies bilingual Armenian/Latin edition, [4], 132, [2] pages.
A 6 May 1636 review/emendation certificate and undated Latin-Armenian comparison certificate precede the 1642 printing; approval and publication dates are distinct.

stages.limitations: Bounded Creed comparison only. Neither a complete diplomatic transcription nor proof of every relationship to earlier Armenian manuscripts. The 1636 certificate does not date the printing or prove the later 1677 book’s complete ancestry.
stages.reception: Published by the Catholic Propaganda Fide for Armenian liturgical use; the extent of local adoption is not established here.

stages.label: Complementary Roman Armenian service books
stages.scope: One complementary set: celebrant’s liturgy and ministers’ directions. The liturgy prints Armenian-form Creed, Nicene anathema and doxology. Ministerium appends corrections to Office and hymns.
stages.witness_label: Խորհրդատետր պատարագին հայոց / Lyturgia Armena (20 pp.) + Սպասաւորութիւն պատարագի / Ministerium Missae (30 pp.)
stages.summary: One complementary set: celebrant’s liturgy and ministers’ directions. The liturgy prints Armenian-form Creed, Nicene anathema and doxology. Ministerium appends corrections to Office and hymns. Its Creed (p. 8) also carries three Western readings: before all ages, consubstantial, and procession of the Spirit from the Father and the Son.

evidence.locus: RA1-PP3 title; RA1-PP14 = Lyturgia p. 8; RA1-PA1 title
evidence.claim: Establishes the native titles, imprint and Creed sequence.
Describes the 20+30-page complementary set; corrections target Office 1667 and hymnal 1664.

Entry 103's collation and woodcut positions match the Google copy; entry 104 is a 50-page continuously paginated impression with a smaller type area, reported as possibly printed later under the 1677 imprint.

A related mixed copy, not attached as a witness of this stage: it shares the title, p. 1 and correction-page settings with the Google copy, and its reset p. 7 prints the same Creed readings (before all ages, consubstantial, procession from the Father and the Son) and the Nicene anathema.

stages.limitations: The two native works are complementary. Ministerium pp. 21–24 correct the Office and pp. 25–30 the hymnal; those appendices do not establish successive Eucharistic versions. The native Lyturgia has twenty numbered pages, with pp. 4–5 rescanned twice. Classification checked 2026-10-22: one textual state in at least two settings. The Google (Angelica) copy is bibliography entry 103. FSL A/711 (EAP) is a mixed copy whose title, pp. 1–6 and corrections share entry 103's settings while pp. 7–19 are reset; at the Creed the reset pages agree with entry 103, so no distinct state is shown there. Cold review 2026-10-22: the EAP copy is not attached as a witness of this stage, because its reset pp. 7–19 carry the anaphora and most of the ordinary, are compared only at the Creed, and are of unknown date and printer; this keeps the 2026-10-20 decision that the copy needs its own approval before stage admission. Entry 104 (50 continuous pages, type area 24 × 16 cm, four woodcuts) is known only from the bibliography, which reports Zarbhanalian's and Ghazikian's view that it was printed much later; no copy has been inspected, and the EAP reset pages cannot be assigned to it (they carry no woodcut and the attached corrections keep entry 103's numbering 21–30). Whether the reset or entry 104 is a later impression is unresolved. Whole-book verbal collation remains incomplete.
stages.reception: Catholic Armenian Roman edition, later explicitly followed by a Mkhitarist Armenian-Church book in 1823; universal use is not inferred.

stages.label: Venice print preserving Apostolic tradition
stages.scope: A separate Armenian missal witness described by scholarship as preserving Armenian Apostolic textual tradition.
stages.witness_label: Խորհրդատետր (Xorhrdatetr), Venice, T‘adēos Hamazaspean and Xoǰa Gaspar Sarhadean, 1686
stages.summary: A separate Armenian missal witness described by scholarship as preserving Armenian Apostolic textual tradition.

evidence.claim: Identifies printing, mixed confessional setting and reported 1691 Roman rejection of the missal’s Apostolic text.

stages.limitations: The critical source describes reception; specific prayers have not been collated here. Its companion lectionary is not automatically part of the existing missal witness ID.
stages.reception: Publisher’s Catholic connections do not establish Roman approval or Armenian Catholic normative reception.

stages.label: Lviv manuscript adjusted toward Roman practice
stages.date_label: Undated later corrections; Mass correction target is Rome 1677
stages.scope: The manuscript bears corrections toward the Roman 1677 Mass and an erased April 7 Annunciation date replaced by March 25.
stages.witness_label: San Lazzaro MS 669 (old 1178), corrected Mass section and altered Annunciation date
stages.summary: The manuscript bears corrections toward the Roman 1677 Mass and an erased April 7 Annunciation date replaced by March 25.

evidence.claim: Cataloguer explicitly describes Mass corrections and the overwritten feast date.

stages.limitations: Hands and dates are not identified. The calendar change and Mass corrections need not be contemporary. No manuscript folio images have been collated.
stages.reception: Evidence for a local manuscript’s correction and reception; no general Roman decree or universal Armenian change follows.

stages.label: Patriarchal Armenian Catholic service book issued for episcopal examination
stages.scope: Patriarchal book identified as using the developed Lambron–Metsop textual family.
stages.witness_label: Խորհրդատետր սրբոյ Պատարագին ըստ արարողութեան Հայաստանեայց եկեղեցւոյ (Vienna: Mekhitarist press, 1879); arar.sci.am copy (lection part); later witness: the patriarchally authorized second printing (Vienna: Mekhitarist press, 1904), Google jJIwAQAAMAAJ
stages.summary: Patriarchal book identified by the official retrospective as using the developed Lambron–Metsop textual family. Its prefixed declaration, signed by Anton Petros IX at Pera on 6 January 1879, says the exemplar was printed so that bishops could examine it and note observations in its margins, pending a national synod and confirmation by the Apostolic See.

evidence.claim: Identifies publication, patriarchal affiliation and textual family.
Native title, Vienna Mekhitarist press and 1879 are directly visible.

evidence.locus: Declaration PDF pp. 6–7, closing paragraphs and dated signature
evidence.claim: Because a council of bishops was hard to assemble, an exemplar of the Mass book was printed for examination with margins for the bishops’ observations, to be agreed at the next synod and submitted for confirmation by the Holy Apostolic See so as to obtain a fixed rule of the Mass; dated Pera, Constantinople, 6 January 1879.
Fourth day of the Nativity: feast of James and John, Epistle 1 John 1:1–7 and Gospel John 21:20–25.
The 1904 Vienna printing carries the same title and reprints the 1879 declaration of Anton Petros IX.

evidence.locus: PP17, patriarchal permission no. 1093, Pera, 17 May 1903
evidence.claim: Paul Peter XI authorizes the Vienna Mekhitarists to make a second printing of the Khorhrdatetr printed at Vienna in 1879 (and of the 1880 Maštocʻ) without change of the text except with his consent, reserving later printings to the patriarch.

evidence.locus: Index PDF 219; printed pp. 19–20 (PDF 15 right, PDF 16 left)
evidence.claim: Nativity and Epiphany have separate sections; the fourth day of Epiphany reads 1 John 5:4–10 with the heavenly witnesses (Father, Word and Holy Spirit) printed in verse 7.
A 1906 survey lists the Hassunian Khorhrdatetr, Vienna 1879 and 1904, as appointing 1 John 5:4–10 for the fourth day of Yaytnutʻiwn.

stages.limitations: The retained scan lacks the 174-page celebrant’s order, so the ordinary’s text and its textual family rest on the retrospective. The declaration presents the book as an examination exemplar; no synodal decision or Roman confirmation of it has been inspected. No 1677-to-1879 revision edge is asserted. Cold review 2026-10-21: the 1904 Vienna printing is recorded here as a later witness of this state, not as a separate station, because its only inspected warrant is a permission for a second printing of the 1879 book without change of the text (except with the patriarch’s consent); no page collation of 1879 and 1904 has been made, and only lections were seen in the 1904 copy. Addendum 2026-10-22: the lection for the fourth day of Epiphany (p. 19) prints the heavenly-witnesses clause of 1 John 5:7; whether earlier Armenian Catholic lection books did so on that day is not compared here, so no lectionary transition is asserted.
stages.reception: Explicitly a patriarchal Armenian Catholic publication, issued for episcopal examination. The patriarch authorized a second printing in 1903 (Vienna 1904), which the 1951 Enciclopedia Cattolica names as the plenary book in Armenian Catholic use (inventory note, not independently verified here).

stages.label: Revised Armenian Catholic order prescribed
stages.scope: A revised order, following manuscript comparison, was prescribed for Armenian Catholic churches from Pentecost 1994.
stages.witness_label: Revised Armenian Catholic Pataragamadoyc‘ prescribed by Catholicos-Patriarch John Peter XVIII in 1994; decree cited in Աւետիք 1994, p. 365
stages.summary: A revised order, following manuscript comparison, was prescribed for Armenian Catholic churches from Pentecost 1994.

evidence.locus: Final paragraphs on 1992 study and 1994 decree
evidence.claim: Reports the revised order and effective reception date, with a precise primary-publication locator.

stages.limitations: Primary decree and definitive book not acquired. Changes to particular prayers and rubrics remain unproved; 1987 demonstration is not treated as a separate edition.
stages.reception: The retrospective reports prescription for all Armenian Catholic churches; implementation beyond the decree is not independently measured.

stages.label: Patriarchal low-Mass book printing the classical text beside a translation
stages.scope: Classical Armenian order of the low Mass printed by the Armenian Catholic Patriarchate with a Western Armenian translation on facing pages.
stages.witness_label: Խորհրդատետր Սուրբ Պատարագի աշխարհաբար թարգմանութեամբ. Թիւ Սուրբ Պատարագ (Zmmar, 2007), classical-text pages
stages.summary: The classical Creed has no procession clause in the Spirit article, reads that is, from the essence of the Father and of the nature of the Father in the Son article, and passes from its last article to the kiss of the altar and the doxology without the Nicene anathema. The intercessions commemorate the Pope.

evidence.locus: Title PDF p. 3; credits PDF p. 4; decree PDF p. 6 (printed 7)
evidence.claim: Patriarchal publication at Zmmar, 2007; decree 279/06 of 7 November 2006 directing the translation for use in parish churches after its acceptance by the bishops’ synod in March 2006.
The vernacular is printed beside the classical text, limited to the low Mass and to a three-year experiment.

evidence.locus: Classical Creed PDF pp. 41 and 43 (printed 42, 44); doxology end PDF p. 45 (printed 46)
evidence.claim: Creed readings and the absence of the anathema are directly visible.
The classical intercessions commemorate the Pope before the patriarch and bishop.

stages.limitations: A low-Mass presentation whose classical source edition is unnamed; it is not shown to reproduce the 1994 book. The admission of the vernacular book as a received service book was deferred by the 2026-10-20 cold check pending evidence of actual use; this stage uses the book only as a dated patriarchal attestation of the classical text. The 2026-10-20 permission register also records it as a book witness rather than a substantive source-language revision; this stage asserts only that the book prints this classical state, not that it introduced it.
stages.reception: Patriarchal publication; the decree directs the translation for parish churches, and the introduction limits it to a three-year trial. Actual use of either column is not independently evidenced.

stages.label: Expanded printing following the Roman 1677 exemplar
stages.scope: An Armenian Eucharistic order expressly following Rome 1677, with expanded supporting texts and a longer presentation.
stages.witness_label: Խորհրդատետր սրբոյ Պատարագին, Venice: San Lazzaro, 1823, Michigan 80-page copy
stages.summary: The title names Rome 1677 as its exemplar. The Creed–Nicene anathema–doxology sequence persists. Psalm and Gospel texts are printed at greater length, and supporting sections surround the service.

evidence.claim: Declared exemplar, retained anathema and expanded displayed text are directly visible.

stages.limitations: A separately dated reception witness, not a demonstrated new normative recension. A structural survey cannot establish every prayer or rubric as identical, and this copy’s exact relation to other 1823 formats remains open.
stages.reception: Mkhitarist San Lazzaro publication expressly claims conformity to Rome 1677; universal Armenian Catholic use is not inferred.

transitions.summary: The Roman Armenian books differ at the Creed: the 1642 Western-form sequence without the Nicene anathema becomes Armenian-form Creed with that anathema in 1677; the doxology remains.

changes.before: Western-form Creed, followed immediately by the doxology after its final Amen.
changes.after: Armenian-form Creed followed by the Nicene anathema before the doxology.
changes.locus_before: Ordo 1642, Google PA46–PA49; Creed continuation and immediate doxology on printed p. 48.
changes.locus_after: Lyturgia Armena 1677, native p. 8, Google RA1-PP14, left column Creed continuing at top right; anathema then doxology in right column.

evidence.claim: No intervening anathema appears between the Creed’s ending and the doxology.
The paragraph beginning Իսկ որք ասեն stands between Creed and doxology.
Independent scholarly comparison identifies the same structural distinction, although its early-edition date is 1646.
Directly fixes the inspected before-state to 1642.
Directly fixes the inspected after-state to the native 1677 book.

transitions.limitations: This is a bounded comparison of published states. It does not prove that the entire 1677 edition was revised directly from the 1642 printing. Ohanjanyan’s 1646 citation remains a bibliographic discrepancy but is no longer the sole basis for the 1642 reading. Exact complete Creed transcription and normalization remain undone. Addendum 2026-10-21: the 1677 Armenian-form Creed still reads before all ages, consubstantial and procession from the Father and the Son (p. 8, image-checked); Armenian-form here means the sequence with the anathema, not a Creed free of Western readings.

transitions.summary: A Lviv Armenian manuscript was altered toward Roman exemplars: its Annunciation heading changed from April 7 to March 25, and its Mass received corrections described as conforming to Rome 1677.

changes.locus_before: MS 669/1178, lectionary additions fols. 476b2–478a1, Annunciation heading.

evidence.claim: Catalogue explicitly describes the erasure and replacement.

changes.before: Passages of the manuscript Mass differed from the Roman 1677 exemplar.
changes.after: Correcting hands altered those passages to agree with that exemplar.
changes.locus_before: MS 669/1178, Mass section beginning fol. 263 (individual correction sites not enumerated).

evidence.claim: Explicit catalogue description of corrections toward the 1677 Roman text.
Records both material alterations in the same manuscript.

transitions.limitations: Not directly collated from manuscript images. The 1636 date belongs to the composite copy, not the correction event; calendar and Mass hands may differ. The calendar alteration is not attributed to the 1677 book. Exact Mass readings are missing.

transitions.summary: The 1823 title declares reception of Rome 1677. Its Creed retains the Nicene anathema while its presentation expands supporting texts.

changes.before: The twenty-page celebrant booklet gives concluding-Gospel direction and incipit.
changes.after: The longer service prints the Gospel bodies John 1:1–14 and John 21:15–22.

evidence.claim: Concluding-Gospel direction and incipit are visible.
The corresponding Gospel bodies are printed.
The title explicitly names the Rome 1677 exemplar.
The Nicene anathema follows the Creed.
The anathema persists, including an image-checked six-word ending agreeing with 1677.

transitions.limitations: The declared exemplar establishes reception of the named edition, not descent from this particular surviving copy. Expanded display of a Gospel does not establish that the 1823 printing introduced its ritual prescription. No whole-book word identity or reform act is asserted.

transitions.summary: Between the printed states of 1823 and 2007 the classical Creed loses its Western readings and the Nicene anathema: the Spirit article no longer has procession from the Father and the Son, the Son article reads from the essence and of the nature of the Father, and the doxology follows the Creed directly.

changes.before: Spirit article includes procession from the Father and the Son.
changes.after: Spirit article has no procession clause.
changes.locus_after: Zmmar 2007 printed p. 44 (PDF p. 43), classical column.

evidence.claim: Reads որ ՚ի Հօրէ եւ յՈրդւոյ բղխի.
Same reading in the 1677 exemplar.
The Spirit article passes from the uncreated and perfect Spirit directly to the Spirit who spoke in the Law.

changes.before: Son begotten only-begotten before all ages, and consubstantial with the Father.
changes.after: Son begotten only-begotten, that is, from the essence of the Father, and of the nature of the Father.
changes.locus_after: Zmmar 2007 printed p. 42 (PDF p. 41), classical column.

evidence.claim: Reads նախ քան զամենայն յաւիտեանս and համագոյակից Հօր.
Reads այսինքն յէութենէ Հօր and ի բնութենէ Հօր.

changes.before: The Nicene anathema stands between the Creed and the doxology.
changes.after: The Creed is followed by the rubric for kissing the altar and the doxology, with no anathema.
changes.locus_before: Venice 1823 p. 41; Rome 1677 Lyturgia p. 8, right column.

evidence.claim: Anathema paragraph beginning Իսկ որք ասենն precedes the doxology.
No anathema between the last article and the doxology.
Inspected before-state.
Inspected after-state in a patriarchal printing of the classical text.
Vienna 1858 celebrant's order still has before all ages, consubstantial, procession from the Father and the Son, and the anathema before the doxology.
The 1880 Vienna clerks' book prints the same three readings and the anathema.
The 1892 Vienna clerks' book prints the same three readings and the anathema.

transitions.limitations: Provisional because the change is located only between printed states: the before-state readings are still printed in Vienna Mekhitarist books of 1858 (celebrant's order), 1880 and 1892 (clerks' books), so in that line the change postdates 1892 (checked 2026-10-22), but the 1879/1904 ordinary and the 1994 book are unseen, so when, by which act and in which book the readings changed is unknown. The 2007 text is a low-Mass presentation. No descent of the 2007 text from the 1823 printing is asserted. The 2007 book is not claimed as the revising edition: the 2026-10-20 permission register retains it as a book witness, not a received operative candidate or a substantive source-language revision; its classical column only attests the later state.

gaps.missing: Manuscript images, folio loci and exact changes from the Xosrov commentary to the later Lambron–Metsop orders; no continuous genealogy. Three manuscripts (San Lazzaro 1411, thirteenth century; Lyon Or. 15, 1314; Munich arm. 6, 1427) are now positioned from Brightman’s description, without inspected texts.
gaps.next_source: Images or catalogue descriptions of Lyon Or. 15, Munich arm. 6 and San Lazzaro 1411; the 1847 Lambronacʻi edition pp. 193–226 (liturgy text from manuscripts of 1306, 1332 and the late seventeenth century, per Brightman xcvi–xcvii), acquired but uncollated; S. Peter Cowe’s Xosrov commentary edition (1991); Gatʻrčean/Tašean 1897 (acquired; its edition of the translated liturgies supports the non-Athanasius anaphoras, not the Athanasius ordinary); Feulner 2001 and Winkler 2005–2013. Further lead (2026-10-22): V. Inglizian, Բնագրական դիտողութիւններ Պատարագամատոյցի մասին, Handēs Amsōreay 62 (1948) nos 1–2, pp. 1–14 and 156–172, on arar.sci.am (not read).
gaps.consequence: Only the identified early anaphora attestation is positioned; broad medieval development is not converted into invented editions.

gaps.missing: Direct complete exemplar genealogy and editorial revision dossier. Ohanjanyan’s 1646 citation (n. 121) gives the same Creed pages 46–49 and the same 1636 Riccardus review and Molino licence as the inspected 1642 book, so it very probably cites this edition or a copy of it; no separate 1646 printing has been found.
gaps.next_source: Propaganda Fide editorial records for the 1636–1642 printing; the second Google 1642 copy mV5VHungd30C for imprint variants; the 1826 Ordo divinae missae armenorum record PCWlMwEACAAJ (132 pages, no preview) to identify its relation to the Roman Ordo.
gaps.consequence: Bounded Creed difference is established; whole-book direct parentage remains unestablished.

gaps.missing: Images and palaeographic dates of correcting hands, original and overwritten Mass passages.
gaps.next_source: San Lazzaro MS 669, old 1178, Mass fol. 263 onward; lectionary fols. 476b2–478a1. Comparative lead (2026-10-22): N. Akinean's catalogue of Armenian manuscripts of Lviv and Stanisławów, Handēs Amsōreay pp. 596–607 (arar.sci.am), for other Lviv service books; it does not describe San Lazzaro MS 669.
gaps.consequence: Calendar and Mass corrections remain catalogue-described; do not assign a fabricated year or join the hands.

gaps.missing: Exhaustive word-level and rubric collation, and comparison of the Michigan 80-page printing with other 1823 formats. The bounded Creed collation extends to the Son and Spirit articles: 1677 p. 8 and 1823 p. 40 agree on before all ages, consubstantial and procession from the Father and the Son. The EAP 1677 copy is now classified (2026-10-22) as a mixed copy whose reset pp. 7–19 agree with the Google copy at the Creed; it is not attached to the 1677 stage until those pages are collated beyond the Creed (cold review 2026-10-22). Who reset those pages, and whether bibliography entry 104 is a later impression, remain open.
gaps.next_source: Acquired 1677 native Lyturgia and 1823 Michigan 80-page witness (the archive.org item khorhrdatetrsrb00unkngoog is the same Michigan copy); LOC 1823 exhibition copy; Armenian bibliography 1801–1850 entries 422–423; a copy of bibliography 1512–1800 entry 104 (the bibliography lists its holding libraries by abbreviation) for its colophon and type; Zarbhanalian's and Ghazikian's bibliographies for the basis of the later dating. Google g_JlAAAAcAAJ and -NQaEX8eIPkC remain unacquired (Google refused access on 2026-10-22).
gaps.consequence: The declared 1677 reception, retained anathema and expanded displayed text are documented; a separate normative reform remains unproved.

gaps.missing: Full LOC manuscript identity, text and reception; the exhibition does not connect it to a Catholic recension.
gaps.next_source: LOC Near East Section item 010, the T‘akhtayghalēn/Sebastia missal copied 1722, and its second 1722 missal (copied near Sebastia and T‘okhat‘ by unknown scribes, per the Library’s 2016 blog post Easter Week Illuminations); Nira Stone and Michael E. Stone, A Pair of Armenian Manuscript Missals in the Library of Congress, Armenian Texts and Studies 2 (Brill, 2019), 114–130, DOI 10.1163/9789004400504_010 (not acquired). A loc.gov search on 2026-10-21 returned HTTP 403 to a scripted client; the digitized LOC missal 2017481355 (Amasya, Eghia Marzvants‘i) is a different manuscript.
gaps.consequence: Catalogued as acquisition leads; not inserted into Catholic succession merely because of proximity to the 1823 exhibit.

gaps.missing: The 1879 and 1904 celebrant's ordinary (absent from the 1879 scan; not located in the 1904 plenary volume) and any component deltas from 1677; the outcome of the episcopal examination and Apostolic See confirmation called for by the 1879 declaration. The Handēs 1906 report is resolved: the 1879 lection for the fourth day of Epiphany (p. 19) prints 1 John 5:4–10 with the heavenly witnesses; the earlier p. 12 check concerned the fourth day of the Nativity, a separate section of this book.
gaps.next_source: The 174-page 1879 ordinary (NLA Yerevan; Vienna Mekhitarists); the 1904 ordinary-only form (Google HS7gzQEACAAJ, 73 pages, no preview; Google refused access on 2026-10-22); the Vienna Mekhitarist press catalogues 1776–1893 and the Armenian Catholic weekly Katʻoghikē Arjagankʻ 1911–1912, both on arar.sci.am, for the examination outcome and the 1911 Rome synod; the synod's acts on the Mass book.
gaps.consequence: 1879 is documented as an examination exemplar; the 1904 printing is recorded as its authorized second printing, a later witness of the same stage rather than a separate station. Their ordinary text and any revision against 1677 remain unproved; the Epiphany lection is documented as a feature of the book, not as a revision.

gaps.missing: Primary promulgation and definitive revised book of 1994, with exact restored or omitted prayers and rubrics. A 2007 patriarchal printing of the classical low-Mass text shows the Creed without the procession clause, the Western Son readings and the anathema; Vienna Mekhitarist books of 1858, 1880 and 1892 still print them, so the change falls between 1892 and 2007 in the evidence seen. Whether 2007 reproduces the 1994 book, and which act or edition made the change, is unestablished.
gaps.next_source: Աւետիք (official monthly of the Armenian Catholic Patriarchate), 1994 p. 365 (not found on arar.sci.am on 2026-10-22); patriarchal/Sacred See liturgical commission documents concluded 1992; the revised Pataragamadoyc‘ effective Pentecost 1994; any twentieth-century Armenian Catholic celebrant's or clerks' book (Vienna, Venice, Bzommar, Beirut) to date the Creed change; the classical source edition used by the 2006 translation commission.
gaps.consequence: The effective 1994 state is documented by official retrospective and a 2007 classical text is documented from the page; the 1994 edition’s own text and the date of the Creed changes are not inferred.
